lastCompletedStory.title: Add the codex models-cache reader behind an injectable DI seam

openQuestions: During this story's own quality-gate run, running two concurrent `bun run check:all` invocations against this repo produced a genuine but non-reproducible-in-isolation failure in test/integration/behavioral-gate.test.ts (a fixed shared tmux socket name, 'cam-it-gate', collided across the two processes). Re-running check:all a single time, in isolation, was fully green (typecheck, 5535/5535 tests, lint, file-size, debt-markers, version-skips, coverage, dead-code, dup, ci-parity, agents-md, test-sleeps all ok, exit 0). This is documented as an operational gotcha in patterns.md (never fire two check:all/bun test invocations concurrently against the same tree), not a product defect in src/config/codex-models-cache.ts or any other source file.
nextStoryContext: src/config/codex-models-cache.ts now exports selectTopCodexModel (pure selector over already-parsed cache JSON: unknown -> CodexModelSelection, filters visibility==='list' && supported_in_api===true, stable-sorts survivors by priority ascending, returns { ok:true; slug } or a structured { ok:false; reason } -- NEVER throws) and readCodexModelsCache (the default production reader, type CodexModelsCacheReader = (path?: string) => CodexModelSelection, defaulting to join(homedir(), '.codex', 'models_cache.json'), mirroring codexAuthCheck's synchronous existsSync/readFileSync point-read idiom). Both are fail-closed on ANY schema drift (not an object, missing/non-array models, a non-object entry, a non-string slug, a non-number priority, or every entry filtered out) -- a partially-valid cache is never partially trusted. The next story (per this story's notes, referenced as US-003 in the prior handoff) is expected to wire readCodexModelsCache into the actual codex dispatch path: turning a not-ok result into either a fallback to the existing project.toml pin, or a fail-closed abort -- neither behavior exists yet, this story only built the reader in isolation with zero call sites wired. Schema fields were confirmed against the openai/codex Rust source (codex-rs/protocol/src/openai_models.rs's ModelInfo struct and the ModelVisibility enum, which serializes 'List'->'list' via #[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]), not just inferred from a sample cache file.

officialDocsValidated.summary: Fetched the ModelInfo struct and ModelVisibility enum from the codex-rs protocol source. Confirmed field names/types match this story's implementation exactly: slug: String, visibility: ModelVisibility, supported_in_api: bool, priority: i32. ModelVisibility is a 3-variant enum (List/Hide/None) with #[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")], confirming 'list' is the correct exact-string comparison for the eligibility filter.
